analysis.description: This research article examines opioid prescribing practices among new users for non-cancer pain across different regions, including the USA, Canada, UK, and Taiwan. It aims to analyze and compare opioid prescribing rates, types, strengths, and initial doses to understand regional differences and potential contributors to the opioid epidemic, highlighting significant variations and trends in prescription practices across the studied countries.

type.justification: The paper presents observational data analysis across different regions to compare opioid prescribing practices.
type.quote: We conducted a retrospective multicenter cohort study of adults who are new users of opioids without prior cancer.
